Nemotron Post-training Calculator

How to use this calculator

  1. Choose the model and GPU in the Model & GPU section. The calculator will populate a starting scenario; review the workload assumptions in the next step before using the estimate.
  2. Refine the customization workload and, if needed, Advanced Configurations. Keep the defaults for an early estimate, or enter the workload and technical settings you expect to use.
  3. Read the results. Review the GPUs needed and estimated wall time. Enter your own hourly GPU rate in the cost card if you also need a compute-cost estimate.

Important: This calculator is intended to provide a directional planning estimate—not a performance guarantee, procurement quote, or service-level commitment.

Calculation trailShow formulas, definitions, units, and where the values come from.

Unit check: achieved compute rate TFLOP/s/GPU ÷ model FLOPs per token GFLOP/token = token throughput tokens/s/GPU.

A FLOP is one floating-point operation. FLOP/s is a compute rate. 1 TFLOP = 1,000 GFLOP. “/GPU” remains in the rate until per-GPU throughput is multiplied by the active GPU count.

    MFU means Model FLOPs Utilization. Reference MFU is recomputed from measured tokens/s/GPU, model FLOPs/token, and the GPU’s dense BF16 peak.

    Speed-assumption sensitivity

    Model FLOPs UtilizationWall timeCost

    Higher Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) means the GPU completes more model math each second, reducing time and compute cost.

    LoRA vs full SFT defaults

    ApproachGPUsTimeCost

    Comparison uses each method’s own dataset-token and epoch defaults plus its verified topology. Full SFT can finish sooner only when its memory-fit topology uses many more GPUs; compare GPU-hours and compute cost as well as wall time.
